title: Interview with Diablo IV 3D Artist, Scarlett Brooks
content:
## _Dive into the creative world of Scarlett Brooks and her journey of crafting iconic characters in Diablo IV._

## _Discover how her background in fashion design and expertise with Marvelous Designer brought unique and personal touches to the game's armor sets._

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/e231aadc618a45ffb22c2ed9193bbb6f/images/774020d523914517a55c4355fe0e8658scarlett-brooks-herald-of-pestilence.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e231aadc618a45ffb22c2ed9193bbb6f/images/5be8901010ce4cf8aa5032dfa6f64b4aezgif-56c7df62fef43c.gif)

* * *

# **Interview with**[**Scarlett Brooks**](https://www.artstation.com/scarlettbrooks3dart)**| 3D Artist**

# **Can you share a bit about yourself and your journey as an artist?**

Hello!

My name is Scarlett Brooks and I was one of the Blizzard 3D artists who worked on DiabloIV. My passion for art started at a young age—before I could even hold a pencil properly, I was already sketching monsters and dreaming up unique clothing designs. Despite my parents' initial reservations, I followed my heart and chose to pursue a career in the creative world, ultimately earning my degree in fashion design.

# **The variety of characters in Diablo IV is fascinating. Which character was your favorite to work on, and why?**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e231aadc618a45ffb22c2ed9193bbb6f/images/78b0102ab2f04e08946cf3022c735980necF_stor179_1.png)

During my time on Diablo IV, I primarily worked on the Necromancer and Sorceress characters. However, the most meaningful armor set I crafted was the "Herald of Pestilence." The concept, created by the incredibly talented Elena Danilova, really resonated with me because it offered the chance to introduce something visually distinct to the world of Sanctuary.

If you take a closer look, you'll notice a small but personal detail: within the little cage on the hip, there's a sculpt of my chinchilla, who passed away around that time. It was my way of honoring his memory and, in a sense, immortalizing him within the game.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e231aadc618a45ffb22c2ed9193bbb6f/images/c6fcc355de024891b9f010a4ea60ec77necM_stor179_1.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e231aadc618a45ffb22c2ed9193bbb6f/images/0e59e38e579145cc856f9f9b1028dd48necM_stor179_blue.png)

# **Could you highlight some of the iconic characters that were brought to life using Marvelous Designer?**

All of the armor sets I worked on were created with the help of Marvelous Designer. If I had to highlight a couple more that really stand out, it would be the "Glory of Yshari" armor and "Reign of Solitude." Both were incredibly rewarding to bring to life!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e231aadc618a45ffb22c2ed9193bbb6f/images/60b0f3ac9ab141aaa72d260aac1a5ebasorc_Yshari_Highpoly.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e231aadc618a45ffb22c2ed9193bbb6f/images/3096261db7894f7bbc71db83fa82054cezgif-5653dca0783389.gif)

# **What led you to incorporate Marvelous Designer into your workflow, and how did it support the art direction for your projects?**

(Jokingly) With my background in fashion design, I may or may not have subtly encouraged the rest of the game pipeline to revolve around using Marvelous Designer. Honestly, I think I was hired for my Marvelous Designer skills, which is why I ended up with all the projects featuring those precious-looking fabrics with lots of folds, twists, and bunching. Sculpting cloth by hand can be tedious, and let’s face it, it doesn’t always turn out as realistic as we'd like!.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e231aadc618a45ffb22c2ed9193bbb6f/images/be912fa0c00d4c47a649ef25c27a4f3b001.png)

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

I’ve always enjoyed creating patterns, and Marvelous Designer, with all its amazing tools, really allows me to bring that passion to life. For me, it’s all about crafting a clean design in the 2D viewport that simulates exactly what I envision. The ability to work with symmetrical patterns is such a time-saver—it lets me focus on creativity while saving hours in the process!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e231aadc618a45ffb22c2ed9193bbb6f/images/ccfabd141b7a493eb50c529c81c42bbe007%282%29.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e231aadc618a45ffb22c2ed9193bbb6f/images/c977fd9f3bc6463b955c375c825daa28Mikasa%20AoT%20-%20Marvelous%20Designer.jpg)

# **What tips do you have for other artists using Marvelous Designer in game development?**

If you’re struggling with creating patterns, try thinking of each piece as a UV island. Consider how and where you’d curve a loop, the edge flow that would best emphasize the shapes you’re aiming for, and always keep the grain direction in mind when manipulating folds. It’s all about approaching the design with the same level of attention you’d give to a 3D model’s surface flow.

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

Marvelous Designer is definitely my favorite part of the pipeline. There’s so much flexibility—it feels like there are a million different ways to achieve great results. The possibilities are endless, and that’s what makes it so exciting to work with.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e231aadc618a45ffb22c2ed9193bbb6f/images/06a3753ef0b14e5ead7d3bc4ef68a8d1Hua-Jian-Meng-Shi-Orange-Costume-Tang-Empress-Ancient-Chinese-Hanfu-Stage-Clothing-Sd-doll-tang.jpg_960x960.png)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e231aadc618a45ffb22c2ed9193bbb6f/images/e0fbc8f65a16422f979adc99b4212ed1HanFu%20-%20Marvelous%20Designer.jpg)
content_description: Explore the artistic journey of Scarlett Brooks, a talented 3D artist behind Diablo IV's iconic characters, as she shares her unique blend of fashion design and digital artistry to create captivating armor sets.

title: Troubleshooting: Auto Fitting and Arrangement Points
content:
# Are you getting these alerts when importing your custom avatar?

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/12dc15957be44852b7ec66959a774353/images/596ac93da385443299075c073c4fbd0eimage.png)

**_"Arrangement points were not fitted to the avatar. The avatar must be in a T-pose or A-pose."_**

_Or  
"_**_Fitting Suit cannot be created._**_The avatar must be in a T-Pose or A-pose"_

There can be a lot of reasons that you might see these errors. First, always best check the "Best Practice Checklist" below and see if it matches what you have so far!

**Best Practice Checklist for Importing Avatars**

  * Avatar is 1 mesh body

  * Avatar has closed geometry (no holes)

  * Avatar is 1,200-2,000 millimeters tall

  * Avatar is in an A-Pose

  * Avatar has 2 arms, 2 legs, 1 head

  * Importing a OBJ or FBX file type

  * Correct normal direction (normals facing outward)




After double checking (or not, it will be covered in the flowchart) we can move onto the flow chart.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/12dc15957be44852b7ec66959a774353/images/c39f3d2fe4514096ad22d1d1f3266a9dimage.png)

If you are stuck or end up in the "contact support" portion. Make sure to contact the software support team of the software you are using: 

  * For Marvelous Designer: <https://marvelousdesigner.com/support/contact>

  * For CLO: [https://www.clo3d.com/en/support](https://www.clo3d.com/en/support)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Thank you! This is super helpful!
content_description: This webpage provides essential troubleshooting tips and best practices for successfully importing custom avatars while addressing common error alerts related to avatar poses and geometry.

title: Copic Brand Promotion
content:
## _From Pixels to Polygons – Explore the journey of a graphic designer who transitioned to 3D design, achieving remarkable results with her first project using Marvelous Designer._

* * *

# **Interview with Yuri Choi | Copic Brand Promotion | 3D Artist**

#   
**We would like to know about you, Yuri. Could you please give a brief introduction and explain how you started working in 3D?**

Hello, I am Yuri Choi, working in 3D in South Korea. Since childhood, I have enjoyed looking at illustrations and drawing, which naturally led me to major in design. After graduation, I got a job at a 3D media art exhibition company as a graphic designer, where I was offered the opportunity to try 3D work as well. This prompted me to start studying 3D in earnest and challenge myself in a new field.

# **Could you please explain in detail about your recent project, "Copic Brand Promotion"?**

The "Copic Brand Promotion" is the first portfolio video I created at the academy where I studied 3D. The theme of this video is "A Parade of Vibrant Colors by Copic Markers that Brighten Up the City." It emphasizes the ease and speed of coloring with Copic markers, depicting shapes representing various marker tips starting from a small space and joyfully spreading color throughout the city. To highlight the advantage of quick coloring, I focused on dynamic and fast-paced scenes. Additionally, I aimed to make the scenes more exciting and lively by synchronizing them with the rhythm of the music.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/392cd325444e4a6cbef2ebc6f2e50c53/images/c5a16e3a1d0e43d68b783b41d5ec4dd9Marker_Detail_04.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/392cd325444e4a6cbef2ebc6f2e50c53/images/a3e2f9bce4c244ee9f98728dfac8dc5aMarker_Detail_02.png)

# **Your work using Marvelous Designer is impressive. Do you have any advice or tips for Marvelous Designer users based on your recent project?**

I used Marvelous Designer to express vibrant colored clothes. First, I modeled a mannequin in C4D to dress it, set the desired rotation speed and direction, and then imported it into Marvelous Designer. Since the design of the clothes I envisioned was relatively simple, I could create it quickly. Through animation, I adjusted the fabric's stretch, weight, and movement during rotation to achieve the desired texture. Once I was satisfied with the clothing motion, I transferred it back to C4D to complete the texturing work.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/392cd325444e4a6cbef2ebc6f2e50c53/images/eaf49f3d4d4745349f5ec09f2a2a83f9Dress%20%282%29.gif)

The biggest issue during this process was the structure of the clothing pattern. The fabric around the waist and neck was supposed to hold the top in place, but the pulling forces caused the clothes to keep slipping off the mannequin's neck. To solve this, I first elongated the mannequin's neck and created a band to secure the shape. I figured that lengthening the neck would reduce the chance of the clothes slipping off. Then, I added a band around the waist to secure it similarly and connected the top to the waist and neck bands.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/392cd325444e4a6cbef2ebc6f2e50c53/images/a0f531e4673e4d339b6c08bfa3805f08Marvelous_02.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/392cd325444e4a6cbef2ebc6f2e50c53/images/7f07163b7d654af3b9295165b62ce9baMarvelous_01.png)

Instead of trying various attempts on the existing mannequin, I quickly modified the modeling to address the root cause of the problem. By applying the results from the modified mannequin to the existing work, I could solve the issue simply and efficiently. Would this method be considered a tip?😊

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/392cd325444e4a6cbef2ebc6f2e50c53/images/afe22d71d915453aae4c54b072605fd1ezgif-2ce3a67752f3a.gif)

# **Could you provide a brief overview of the various tools used in your pipeline?**

In addition to Marvelous Designer, I mainly used Cinema4D, Octane Render, After Effects, Photoshop, and Illustrator. Photoshop and Illustrator were used to create the necessary source images. The overall layout composition and rendering work were done in Cinema4D and Octane. The rendered images were then brought into After Effects for final post-processing to complete the final video.

# **When working on a project, there must be parts you enjoy the most and parts that are challenging. What was the most enjoyable part of the process for you?**

I found the most enjoyment in the process of setting up style frames for each scene. Moving from the storyboard stage to actually setting up the lighting and post-processing to beautifully complete the scenes felt like a special experience of bringing imagination to reality.

I particularly remember the initial concept for the scene featuring a vibrant-colored dress. I was unsure about what kind of dress to create and which colors to choose, but then I had the idea to use AI. I first created a simple reference image and then used AI to add details and refine the image. After that, I found a similar clothing pattern and created the dress in Marvelous Designer.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/392cd325444e4a6cbef2ebc6f2e50c53/images/0b9a80dccb274b57b778a0172e7d9d6dDress_ref.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/392cd325444e4a6cbef2ebc6f2e50c53/images/eb3379ba3e9246f986c3279fb73b185aAI_01.png)

  
This was my first time using Marvelous Designer, and I remember trying various things and going through trial and error without watching any guide tutorials. Looking back, I wonder why I didn't look up resources from the start, but I clearly remember how much fun I had and how focused I was on the work. The process of using AI to refine my ideas and boldly trying out Marvelous Designer was the most interesting and enjoyable part of the project.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/392cd325444e4a6cbef2ebc6f2e50c53/images/bc7f165a2f7e4c7cbb14336327338ac8Dress_Before.png)

# **What was the biggest challenge you faced while working on the project?**

The biggest challenge was having to control all aspects of the work by myself. As a beginner, handling everything from modeling, lighting, sound editing, sound effects, and post-processing alone was very complex and overwhelming.

Another major difficulty was figuring out effective ways to express my ideas. For example, when creating the scene where a blue store appears after the marker shape passes through an alley, I spent a long time staring at the monitor, unsure of how to make it look natural. Initially, I tried to show ink droplets seeping into the wall to create the store, but the result didn't feel right, so I changed direction. I then came up with the idea to layer colors gradually, similar to how markers are used, to reveal the store's vibrant texture. Ultimately, I created a scene where 2-3 layers with the marker's transparent and vivid texture overlapped to form the store, which received positive feedback for being impressive.

The process of figuring out how to effectively portray the desired look was always challenging but also very rewarding.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/392cd325444e4a6cbef2ebc6f2e50c53/images/40e4b2ce826245aeb636b282922d6478Store.gif)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/392cd325444e4a6cbef2ebc6f2e50c53/images/2de31df6657f4cee9c3ad3b48b0105faStreet.gif)

# **Lastly, do you have any advice for those starting out in 3D art? It could be career advice or mindset tips for creating artwork.**

Don't doubt yourself, and if you do, shake it off quickly!

I often doubted myself or questioned my talent. But recently, I recalled my early days in 3D. I remembered the excitement of holding the mouse and working enthusiastically on a simple model with a basic texture. I have grown a lot since then, and I continued working with the belief that I could improve even more.

There are times when I get stuck or struggle to come up with ideas, but the sense of accomplishment and rapid progress when the results turn out better than expected are truly precious. If you can recall these positive experiences more vividly and for longer than any negative thoughts about yourself, I believe you can work much more healthily.

Of course, it's important to identify and address your shortcomings, but sometimes taking the time to reflect on your strengths and progress so far can give you the motivation to create even more beautiful artwork.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/392cd325444e4a6cbef2ebc6f2e50c53/images/8a05b56b388a4159b9ee7eb9544398cdDress_Final.png)
content_description: Discover the inspiring journey of graphic designer Yuri Choi as she transitions to 3D design, showcasing her innovative project using Marvelous Designer and offering valuable insights for aspiring artists.
